articles.title: 12th-Class Boy Abducted From Bus, Framed With 2.7 KG Opium: Madhya Pradesh Police Exposed
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking case has emerged from Madhya Pradesh involving a 12th-grade student from Rajasthan who was abducted, falsely implicated, and jailed on fabricated drug charges. The Madhya Pradesh High Court has now acquitted him and sharply reprimanded the police officials involved.

body.html:
A shocking case has emerged from Madhya Pradesh involving a 12th-grade student from Rajasthan who was abducted, falsely implicated, and jailed on fabricated drug charges. The Madhya Pradesh High Court has now acquitted him and sharply reprimanded the police officials involved.

On 28 August, Sohanlal, a Class 12 student from Jodhpur, visited Mandsaur to see the Pashupatinath Temple. While he was travelling in a bus, a Scorpio overtook the vehicle and stopped it. Three youths got down, dragged Sohanlal out of the bus, forced him into the Scorpio, and drove away.

Two days later, on 30 August, Malhargarh police arrested him and sent him to jail, claiming he was caught with 2.7 kg of opium.

Meanwhile, Sohanlal’s family searched for the bus he had boarded. When they located it, they checked the CCTV footage installed inside. The truth was clear: Sohanlal had been forcibly taken away. His father then approached the Indore High Court with this evidence.

On 5 December, the High Court acquitted Sohanlal and strongly criticised the police. SP Vinod Meena was summoned, and police station in-charge Rajendra Panwar, sub-inspector Sanjay Pratap Singh, Sadik Mansoori, and constables Narendra, Jitendra, and Dilip were suspended.

Sohanlal stated that the policemen had demanded Rs 12 lakh from him and, when he refused to pay, they implicated him in a false narcotics case.

articles.title: Pakistani Woman vs Long-Term Visa Husband: Explosive Allegations Rock Indore
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A Karachi resident named Nikita has approached the Indore High Court seeking action against her Pakistani-origin husband, Vicky Nagdev, who has been living in Indore on a long-term visa.

body.html:
A Karachi resident named Nikita has approached the Indore High Court seeking action against her Pakistani-origin husband, Vicky Nagdev, who has been living in Indore on a long-term visa. Nikita alleges that Vicky abandoned her at the Attari border in 2020 under the pretext of visa processing and has since been living illegally in India. She claims he is now preparing to remarry without divorcing her.

According to the petition, the couple married in January 2020. A few months later, Vicky allegedly took Nikita to the Wagah–Attari border and left her there, promising to call her back. She states that he has been untraceable since then. Nikita has also submitted complaints to the PMO seeking action.

Meanwhile, Vicky denies all charges. He claims he has been living legally in India and accuses Nikita of blackmail. He alleges that she repeatedly demanded money and refused to return to India despite multiple requests.

The High Court will now examine the allegations from both sides, including claims of illegal stay, abandonment, and blackmail. The matter has drawn significant attention due to cross-border marital complications and visa irregularity concerns.

articles.title: Second Marriage Scam? Singrauli Woman Accuses Husband of Cheating, Theft and Abuse
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman from Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh, has levelled serious allegations against her second husband, claiming she was deceived, looted and later assaulted.

body.html:
A woman from Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh, has levelled serious allegations against her second husband, claiming she was deceived, looted and later assaulted. Government employee Amreen Ahmed, originally from Varanasi, married Avinash Yadav of Ghazipur on 29 February 2024 under the Special Marriage Act after the two met and developed a relationship through social media.

According to Amreen, Avinash entered her life years after her first husband’s death, and she believed he would support her and her two children. However, she alleges that Avinash concealed the fact that he was already married. After their court marriage, she claims he took all her savings, jewellery, gold, and even the money she had received after her first husband’s death.

Amreen further alleges that after taking her assets, Avinash began doubting her character and physically assaulting her. She claims he lived with her for three years, but once she confronted him over his behaviour, he abandoned her.

The woman has now approached Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at the Janta Darbar, seeking justice. She states that CM Yogi has assured her that action will be taken. Amreen has demanded that Avinash return her assets and face legal consequences.

She also alleges that Avinash is currently absconding with his first wife and continues to threaten her over the phone. Amreen has registered a case against him at Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh.

articles.title: Maharashtra: Bike Gangs Loot Moving vehicle on NH-52, Viral Video Triggers Massive Police Crackdown
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Authorities in Maharashtra’s Beed district have intensified patrols and launched targeted operations after a surge in robberies and bag-snatching incidents along the Solapur–Dhule highway, especially between Pachod and Yedshi.

body.html:
Authorities in Maharashtra’s Beed district have intensified patrols and launched targeted operations after a surge in robberies and bag-snatching incidents along the Solapur–Dhule highway, especially between Pachod and Yedshi.

According to officials, groups of robbers have been stopping passenger vehicles, threatening commuters, and stealing luggage, prompting police to issue safety advisories to travellers.

A video of one such highway robbery has gone viral on social media, with users claiming it was recorded last month on National Highway 52 near Beed. The footage, reportedly captured from a bus-mounted camera, shows five to six bike-borne men trailing the vehicle. One of them climbs onto another’s shoulder and manages to board the rear of the moving bus. He is seen opening the luggage compartment, pulling out bags, and throwing them onto the road. He later jumps off when the driver slows down after sensing something suspicious.

Police stated that similar crimes have been reported recently in Beed and neighbouring areas, leading to increased night patrols and trap deployments. Alerts have also been circulated via local WhatsApp groups to warn the public and coordinate with police units across the region.

Hotel and lodge owners along the highway have been instructed to ensure functional CCTV systems and share relevant footage promptly. Food vendors and accommodation providers have been asked to cooperate with the investigation. Contact details of key police personnel have been distributed to establishments for quicker communication.

Authorities have also launched awareness campaigns, putting up posters and issuing guidelines urging travellers to avoid halting on the highway at night. Police say heightened surveillance and community participation are helping in efforts to identify and apprehend the culprits while maintaining strict vigilance along the route.

articles.title: Raipur DSP Love-Trap Scandal: Businessman Looted of ₹2.5 Crore? Shocking Allegations
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A complaint filed at Raipur’s Khamhardih police station has triggered major unrest within the Chhattisgarh police department.

body.html:
A complaint filed at Raipur’s Khamhardih police station has triggered major unrest within the Chhattisgarh police department. Businessman Deepak Tandon has accused State Police Service officer and Dantewada-posted DSP Kalpana Verma of blackmail, bribery and threats—allegedly carried out through a fabricated love affair.

DSP Kalpana Verma, a 2016–17 batch officer and former CSP as well as DSP-ATS of Mana police station, is accused of duping the businessman of more than ₹2.5 crore on the pretext of marriage. Deepak has submitted WhatsApp chats and CCTV footage as evidence. He claims he was threatened with false criminal cases if he did not withdraw his complaint. Police reportedly delayed the investigation citing the high-profile nature of the case. Both sides have now filed FIRs against each other.

According to Deepak, during their two-year relationship, he transferred ₹2.5 crore to the DSP through bank and online payments. The amount allegedly includes a ₹12-lakh diamond ring, a ₹10-lakh bracelet, gold jewellery worth ₹5 lakh each, and expensive clothing and shopping expenses.

He further alleges that he was pressured into registering Atmospheria Hotel on VIP Road in the name of Kalpana’s brother, despite paying a major amount himself. Deepak claims the DSP invested only ₹30 lakh but got the property registered in her name. Additionally, a Toyota Hyryder worth ₹22 lakh—registered in Deepak’s wife Barkha’s name—was allegedly taken over by the DSP. Barkha has submitted a complaint seeking protection for her husband.

Media reports indicate that Kalpana enjoyed significant influence during the previous Congress regime. Her transfer to Bastar, along with 38 other DSPs, was reportedly cancelled, allowing her to retain a senior posting in Raipur. Sources claim senior IPS officers, including Sheikh Arif, played a role in altering the transfer orders. Although the BJP government eventually moved her to Dantewada, reports allege she continued using luxury government vehicles without number plates in Raipur. She is also informally linked to multiple illegal property and financial dealings, though these claims remain unverified.

Despite the complaint being pending for a long time, the police station in-charge allegedly refused to act. Senior officers including the SP and ADG have maintained that protection protocols are being followed. Deepak continues to appeal to senior officials and prominent citizens for justice. Meanwhile, the DSP’s brother has filed a counter-complaint against Deepak. Insiders claim romantic entanglements within police circles often arise, but the situation is now escalating into criminal disputes.

DSP Kalpana Verma has denied all allegations, calling them “false, baseless and part of a conspiracy” to damage her career. Speaking to Bansal News, she said she is prepared to cooperate with any inquiry and asserted confidence that the truth will emerge.

articles.title: Engineer Murdered Over Alleged Abuse, Control and Property Dispute in Lucknow
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking case from Lucknow, disturbing details have surfaced in the murder of 33-year-old engineer Surya Pratap Singh, who lived in a live-in relationship with 46-year-old Ratna.

body.html:
In a shocking case from Lucknow, disturbing details have surfaced in the murder of 33-year-old engineer Surya Pratap Singh, who lived in a live-in relationship with 46-year-old Ratna. During interrogation, Ratna told police that Surya had allegedly touched her elder daughter inappropriately, which triggered the fatal attack.

According to police, Ratna and her two daughters assaulted Surya with a knife, killing him on the night of 7 December. Investigators are examining multiple angles, including allegations that the murder was committed to gain control over the house.

Key Motives Under Investigation

1. Alleged misbehaviour with elder daughter
Ratna alleged that Surya misbehaved with her elder daughter and assaulted her when she resisted. On 7 December, he allegedly dragged the girl into a room after seeing a photo on her phone. Ratna and her younger daughter intervened, and Ratna stabbed Surya multiple times in the neck, leading to his death.

2. Confinement and control
Police stated that Surya kept Ratna’s daughters under tight surveillance, monitoring them through three CCTV cameras. He restricted their social media activity and delayed the elder daughter’s education, getting her admitted to Class 12 only this year. This prolonged control reportedly built resentment in the family.

3. Property dispute
Surya lived in a house constructed on his land, while Ratna claimed she had financed the construction using money from her late husband. Frequent arguments reportedly took place over transferring the property and a car into her name.

Surya, a resident of Jankipuram, had met Ratna in 2012 while tutoring her daughters. After separating from her alcoholic husband Rajendra, who died in 2014, Ratna moved in with Surya. Two years ago, Surya built a house in Green City, Salarganj, where all four lived together.

Surya’s father alleged that Ratna and her daughters benefited from his son’s earnings, while Surya had been considering marriage elsewhere. He had spoken to his father and sent him money on 7 December, hours before the incident.

Sequence of events
– Around 9 AM on 8 December, Ratna called police and confessed to murdering Surya.
– She claimed the murder took place at 11 PM on 7 December and the body remained in the room overnight.
– Police arrested Ratna and her daughters following a complaint filed by Surya’s father, Narendra Singh.

Police said Ratna showed no remorse during questioning. She receives a monthly pension of Rs 35,000 from her late husband’s service in the Census Department and admitted she wanted the house transferred to her name to secure her position if Surya ever left.

Surya was the only son of his parents. His father works as a driver at Max Hospital, his mother is a homemaker, and he has two married sisters. Ratna reportedly has no connection with her late husband’s family.
